text: This tadka is oil-free. Ingredients include date paste, imli (tamarind), curry leaves, green chili, mustard seeds, and hing (asafoetida). All ingredients are added to boiling water and then poured over the dhokla.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: For vegan tea with oat milk, consider these WFPB notes: (1) Instead of the “Oatly” brand for oat milk, choose “Three Trees” brand (often found in Grocery Outlet for cheap) as Oatly has oil as an ingredient, while Three Trees has a much better ingredient list. (2) Instead of agave syrup, honey, or jaggery (all classified as “Added Sugars”), use homemade date syrup or date paste as a sweetener (dates, date syrup, date sugar & date paste are recommended by Dr. Greger; raisins, dried figs, etc., can also be used for sweetening preparations other than chai).

recipe_name: Understanding Dr. Michael Greger and WFPB Principles
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Dr. Michael Greger is a prominent figure in Whole Food Plant-Based (WFPB) nutrition. His website, NutritionFacts.org, hosts over 2,000 short videos on nutrition, providing scientific reasoning for WFPB guidelines. He is the author of the bestseller “How Not To Die” and “How Not To Die Cookbook,” which is SOS-Free (without Salt, Oil, and Sugar), using ingredients like miso for salty flavor. Dr. Greger is a Fellow and founding member of the American College of Lifestyle Medicine (ACLM), a medical specialization focusing on lifestyle, particularly 100% vegan WFPB nutrition, free from oil, sugar, ultra-processed foods, and refined grains. He shares his personal story in a 3-minute video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9Z-gKAvzOY). For discussions on personal health markers, medical conditions, macro-nutrients, and micro-nutrients, members are encouraged to join the “WFPB Chit Chat” group.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
For the cheese layer: Blend 1 cup soaked cashews, 1 block silken tofu, 1/2 block firm tofu, 1/2 cup soy yogurt, 1/2 cup date syrup, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 tsp pure vanilla extract, 1 tsp agar agar (soaked in room temp water for 10 minutes, then boiled in a pan until it begins to form a gel – psyllium husk could also work), and the rind and juice of one large lemon until smooth. Pour over the base layer and freeze for 3-4 hours or overnight.
For the base layer: Blend 1/2 cup walnuts, 1/2 cup pecans (or replace with walnuts), 1/4 cup almonds, 10 mejdool dates, and 1/2 cup roasted almond flour in a food processor until it resembles breadcrumbs. Do not add water. Press evenly into a thin layer on a springform pan and freeze for a couple of hours.
For the mango layer: Blend 1 cup each of 1/2 frozen Kesar mango pulp from India and 1/2 fresh mangoes until smooth. Pour on top of the 'cheese' layer and freeze for another couple of hours. Decorate with cut mango cubes and slivered almonds. Bring the cheesecake to the fridge an hour before serving.

text: Kanji is a good probiotic drink that can be made year-round. It is considered more palatable than kombucha, which often contains sugar.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: Raw mixed diced or shredded veggies (carrot, beet, cabbage, turnip, etc.) OR boiled diced potatoes. Water, salt, turmeric, hing, black mustard powder, red chili powder, ACV (apple cider vinegar). Optional: grated ginger. Method: Boil water, and when it’s warm, add salt, turmeric, hing, black mustard powder, red chili powder & ACV. Leave it on the countertop. You can add the veggies the same day or the next day. Optional to add grated ginger. Cover the jar with a cloth & keep in the sun for a few hours (if possible). It will start to turn sour on day 3-4. Keep checking & start using. Once it is sour enough, keep it outside for a day or two & then move leftovers to the fridge.

text: Amaranth pudding (with sweet fruits and cardamom powder) is a favorite preparation. For potlucks, add sweeteners like chopped dates, chopped dried figs, frozen sweet cherries, a little bit of cacao powder, slivered almonds (and other nuts like pistachios). You may add some dates or dried figs or date syrup or date sugar for extra sweetness. The buckwheat is eaten raw after overnight soaking and rinsing.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 1 cup Rajgira (Amaranth) flour, 1 large steamed Sweet potato (Japanese or regular), 1 carrot grated (hand grate for easy blending), a handful of arugula leaves chopped fine, a handful of cilantro leaves chopped fine, chilies chopped fine according to taste, peanut or pecan powder, salt to taste. Method: Mash the sweet potato well, add all the ingredients and mix well into a ball. If it’s too mushy, add some more amaranth flour. Split into 4-6 portions. Heat the tava (cast iron, seasoned with oil and wiped away). With wet hands, either pat each portion one by one directly on the tava, or pat it into a thalipeeth on a silicon mat and gently lift to place on the tava. Cover and let it cook for 2-3 minutes. Flip it and let the other side cook. Enjoy warm with chutney.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 1 large Granny Smith apple, a large handful cilantro, chillies to taste, 1 clove garlic, a handful of roasted peanuts or pecans, salt. Method: Grind all ingredients in a blender until smooth.

creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text: Ingredients: 1 Chinese eggplant, 2 roasted garlic cloves, 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp parsley, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp tahini, 1/4 cup yogurt, 1/8 tsp salt. Method: Roast eggplant and peel off skin. Mash and add all ingredients.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 1/2 cup tri-colored quinoa, 4 tbsp chana daal, 3 tbsp toor daal, 3 tbsp moong daal, 1/2 cup spinach, 2 green chillies, 1/2 inch ginger, 1 tsp garam masala powder (to taste), 1 tsp coriander+cumin powder (to taste), 1/3 tsp turmeric powder, Himalayan salt to taste, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 chopped carrot, 1/4 cup green peas, 1/4 cup chopped green beans, 2 chopped garlic cloves. Method: 1. Rinse and soak quinoa and daals for 30 minutes. 2. Blanch the spinach, add green chillies and ginger, then grind to a paste. 3. Pressure cook the soaked quinoa+daals+turmeric powder and salt until soft (5 minutes after the first whistle). 4. In a pot, dry temper the cumin, add garlic, and sauté for a minute. 5. Add peas and carrots, cook for 5 minutes. 6. Add the pureed spinach, stir, cook for 1-2 minutes, then add garam masala, coriander, and cumin powder. Now add the cooked quinoa+daals and stir. 7. Turn off the heat and enjoy!

text: For optimum sweetness in pistachio cake, increase the sweetener quantity to 1.5 times the original recipe. If the cake is not sweet enough, it can be transformed into a Tres Leches cake by adding date syrup to your choice of plant-based milk and pouring it over the cake.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 4 medium bananas, 30 toothpicks. Chocolate sauce: 12 soaked dates, 2 tbsp cacao powder, 2/3 cup water, 6 tbsp date syrup, 2 tbsp almond butter. Toppings: Popped Amaranth (or other suggestions below). Method: 1. Peel bananas, cut into thick slices, insert toothpicks, and freeze for 2-3 hours. 2. For the chocolate sauce, soak dates in 2/3 cup hot water for 30 minutes. 3. Blend soaked dates and water to a smooth paste, adding more water if needed. 4. In a pot, add date syrup to 1/4 cup water and cook on low heat until slightly thickened. 5. Add the blended chocolate date mix and almond butter to the pot. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes. 6. Turn off heat, let the chocolate sauce cool, then pour into a glass bowl. 7. Dip each frozen banana slice into the sauce, then gently roll into popped amaranth or sprinkle with chopped nuts. 8. Drizzle extra sauce on the pops, freeze for 20 minutes, and serve. Additional topping suggestions: 2 tbsp roasted and crushed pistachios, 2 tbsp roasted and crushed peanuts, 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 1 tsp active dry yeast, 1 tsp maple syrup, 2 1/4 cups + 2 tbsp whole wheat flour (e.g., One Degree Organic Sprouted Whole Wheat Flour). Method: 1. Measure 1 1/4 cups warm (105F) water, stir in yeast and maple syrup. Cover and place in a dark place for 1-2 hours until foamy and cloudy. 2. In a medium bowl, stir together 2 1/4 cups flour. Stir the yeast mixture into the flour until a batter-like dough forms. Stir vigorously for 30 seconds until smooth. Cover and chill dough overnight. 3. Two hours before baking, line an 8-inch square baking pan with parchment paper, dusting with 2 tbsp flour. Pour chilled dough into the pan. Cover with a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until doubled in volume. 4. Preheat oven to 425 F. Using damp fingers, press dimples all over the top of the focaccia. Add seasonings like Italian seasoning and Herbes de Provence. 5. Bake for 35-40 minutes or until browned and firm on top. Use parchment paper to remove from pan; cool on a wire rack. Peel away parchment paper once cool enough to handle. Cool completely before serving. The texture of the bread was soft to the touch.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 3/4 packet spaghetti (cooked per instructions), 4 chopped garlic cloves, 1/2 chopped red onion, 1/4 chopped yellow squash, 5 chopped baby portabella mushrooms, 2 chopped tomatoes, 2 medium chopped carrots, 1 tbsp 21 Salute seasoning, 1 tbsp Italian seasoning, 2 tsp dried parsley, 3-4 tbsp salt-free tomato paste. Method: 1. Dry sauté garlic and onions in a pan, adding water if needed, until translucent. 2. Add the rest of the veggies, cook with a lid on until slightly softened. 3. Add chopped tomatoes and tomato paste, stir, and cook with a lid on until tomatoes soften. 4. Remove lid, add all herbs, and cook until the sauce comes together and water dries up a little. 5. Stir in the cooked pasta, adding some pasta water if it looks too dry. 6. Enjoy! Notes: Bell pepper, zucchini, and edamame can also be added. Use herbs of your choice.

Method: Blend all ingredients until smooth. Chill in the fridge for an hour. Toppings: cocoa nibs, raspberry, nuts, coconut strips, etc.

text: Ingredients: 1 cup ragi flour, 5-6 large ripe bananas, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda, 1/4 tsp salt, ¼ cup walnuts/pecans/almonds chopped or crushed, 1/4 cup plant yogurt, 1/4 cup lukewarm water (can be replaced with vegan milk). Extra walnuts/pecans/almonds or sugar-free chocolate for garnish. Method: Bake at 350 F for 25-30 minutes. If using a smaller oven, cover the top with a piece of parchment or foil after 20 minutes to prevent burning.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Microwaving is considered acceptable in Whole Food Plant-Based circles. Dr. Greger has videos that provide assurance on this topic (https://nutritionfacts.org/?s=microwave). For example, all of my cooked meals during the last 2-3 years were prepared in a microwave.
